tips.intro: Test Tubes. Water Sort is a color sorting puzzle where you pour layers of liquid between tubes until each tube holds one color. These tips come from clearing Levels 1 and 2 and looking at Level 3, including what the reset and hint buttons really do.
tips: Only the top layer of a tube can move, and it can only land on the same color or in an empty tube. Trying to pour pink onto a blue top did nothing at all.
Use the empty tubes as parking spots. On Level 2, the pinks went into one empty tube and the blues into the other, which uncovered the greens underneath.
Build each color on a tube that already has that color at the bottom. On Level 2 the second tube had two greens at its base, so every loose green went there.
Do not use the curved arrow as an undo. On Level 2 it put the whole level back to its starting layout after two pours.
The light bulb makes one correct pour for you. Its badge dropped from 5 to 4 after one use and stayed at 4 on the next level, so save it.
A tube is finished when it holds 4 layers of one color. A cork drops onto it and a green check mark appears, so you can stop watching it.
Click one tube, wait for the pour animation to end, then make the next move. Slow, separate clicks worked every time in testing.
tips.conclusion: Clear the top layers into empty tubes, stack each color on the tube that already has it at the bottom, and keep the light bulb for real dead ends. There is no clock, so take your time.

extra_sections.heading: A full solve of Level 2
paragraphs: Level 2 has three full tubes on top and two empty tubes below. Reading top to bottom, the first tube is pink, blue, green, pink, the second is pink, blue, green, green, and the third is blue, green, pink, blue.

Pour both top pinks into the first empty tube and the three blues that come to the top into the second empty tube. Then move the greens onto the second tube, which already has two greens at its base. The pinks and the last blue then go to their own tubes, and all three colors get a cork.

controls.intro: Test Tubes. Water Sort uses only mouse clicks. Every move is two clicks: one on the tube you pour from and one on the tube you pour into.
controls.desktop: Click a tube with the left mouse button, then click the tube you want to pour into. The top layer pours across if the move is allowed. If it is not, nothing moves. The buttons along the bottom and the arrows on the menus are clicked the same way. No keyboard keys were used.
tips: The curved arrow at the bottom left restarts the whole level.
The light bulb makes one correct pour for you and started with 5 uses.
Next to it is a tube with a plus sign, also showing 5. It was not pressed during testing.
The double arrow button has a small video icon on it. It was not pressed during testing.
The gear in the top right opens music and sound buttons with an X to close, and the arrow in the top left goes back.

beginner-guide.intro: New to Test Tubes. Water Sort? This walks through the menus, the first two levels and what each button did when it was tried.
beginner-guide.what_it_is: Test Tubes. Water Sort is a free browser puzzle about sorting colored liquid. Each tube holds up to 4 layers. You pour the top layer of one tube into another tube that is empty or has the same color on top, and the goal is to finish with every color alone in its own tube. A sorted tube gets a cork and a green check mark, and a Victory ribbon with up to three stars ends the level. No timer or move counter was seen.
first_steps: Click OK, PLAY NOW! on the loading screen, then the large green play button on the title screen.
On the Select level (1-20) screen, pick level 1. The other levels show padlocks at first.
Level 1 has four tubes with purple and green. Pour the single purple onto the purple tube and the single green onto the green tube.
On the Victory screen, click the right arrow to move to the next level.
On Level 2, use the two empty tubes to hold top layers while you dig out the colors underneath.
beginner-guide.who_its_for: Players who want a slow, quiet puzzle they can stop and start. Early levels are short, and later ones add more colors and tubes.

extra_sections.heading: How the levels grow
paragraphs: Level 1 has four tubes, two colors and no empty tube. Level 2 has three full tubes, three colors and two empty tubes. Level 3 jumps to seven tubes: five full ones in pink, blue, purple, green and red, plus two empty ones.

extra_sections.heading: Stars on the Victory screen
paragraphs: Level 1, solved in two pours, gave three gold stars. Level 2, on a run that used the restart button once and the light bulb once, gave two of three stars. The Victory screen has a list button, a replay button and a right arrow for the next level.

similar.intro: Test Tubes. Water Sort is about untangling mixed colors with very little free space. You can only move the top layer, it has to land on a matching color or in an empty tube, and an empty tube is the most valuable thing on the board. Fans of that kind of slow, careful sorting will feel at home with other water sort and color sort puzzles on Pixelsprout, such as Sort Color Water Puzzle, Mermaid Water Sort and Water Sort - Color Puzzle Game. Look for games with no timer and levels that add colors bit by bit.

faqs.question: How do you pour in Test Tubes. Water Sort?
faqs.answer: Click the tube you want to pour from, then click the tube you want to pour into. The top layer moves across if the target is empty or has the same color on top.

faqs.question: Why will a tube not pour?
faqs.answer: The colors do not match. Pouring a pink top onto a blue top did nothing. Only an empty tube or a matching top color will take the layer.

faqs.question: Is the curved arrow an undo button?
faqs.answer: No. On Level 2 it restarted the whole level, putting every tube back to its starting colors after two pours had been made.

faqs.question: What does the light bulb do?
faqs.answer: It makes one correct pour for you. On Level 2 it moved a green onto the tube that already held two greens, and its badge went from 5 to 4.

faqs.question: How many layers does a tube hold?
faqs.answer: Four. When a tube has four layers of one color, a cork drops on top and a green check mark appears.

faqs.question: How many stars can you get on a level?
faqs.answer: Up to three. Level 1 gave three stars. Level 2 gave two on a run that used the restart button and one hint.

faqs.question: Are all levels open from the start?
faqs.answer: No. The Select level (1-20) screen showed level 1 open and the rest locked with padlocks. Clearing a level opens the next one.

faqs.question: Is there a timer?
faqs.answer: No timer or move counter was seen on any of the first three levels, so you can think each pour through.
